notes: Spanish read by an English speaker, on the standard method. Spanish already ships a bespoke cognate score built from a hand-written suffix table, and that one lives on its own scale for its own slider — the two never meet, because each known language excludes on its own cutoff. This map gives Speech mode a filter it has never had, the legacy flags being present only in artist data. Threshold 0.70. Cutoff 0.75, held after the move to a dictionary-wide map built from the Spanish Wiktionary extract: 147 of the 2,000-card deck (7%), 4,145 of 21,418 scored surfaces. 0.75-0.80 is 55 words and reads almost perfectly (acceso/access, agente/agent, cliente/client, crimen/crime, camara/camera), while 0.70-0.75 is where it goes (compania/companion, emergencia/emergence, campo/camp). One trap leaks: carpeta scores 0.79 against carpet when it means folder. It is kept rather than raising the cutoff to 0.80, which would cost those 55 to block it — the two words are genuinely related and the learner can see why it was set aside, which is the trade this cutoff makes. That is the opposite call to French, where preservatif at 0.76 is worth paying for. Fifteen other standard traps are clear: embarazada 0.14, sensible 0.61, asistir 0.52, sopa 0.46, and exito, ropa, realizar, libreria, actualmente, once, red and pie find no match at all. 2026-09-28: the surface scorer moved to edit-distance/v1 (decision 0027, provisional) and cognate mode became per sense (decision 0028). The cutoff above was carried over, not recalibrated; the calibration figures earlier in this note were measured on the legacy scorer.
